## Context
ADR 0100 makes the immutable route registry and parser factories the authority for command identity, grammar, and committed help. Twenty-one visible pure-intercept routes support `rebar <command> --help` but remain absent from overview help and fail under `rebar help <command>`.

## Plan
- Make the help-backed predicate exactly `not route.hidden and not route.retired` in all four current census sites: `scripts/gen_cli_help.py::_help_backed`, `src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py::_help_backed`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py::_routable_subcommands`, and `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py::_help_backed_nested_families`. Do not add Route metadata.
- Expand the import-safe runtime `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` set to exactly `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, and `workflow`. The argparse-backed families own populated subparsers, while `config validate` is a handler-dispatched pseudo-subcommand with no populated `_SubParsersAction`, so `config` cannot be discovered by parser introspection and must be explicit. A non-leading child `--help` must still reach the owning child parser or handler. Keep the bridge-factory derivation in `_NESTED_FAMILY` unchanged.
- Keep the parameterized nested-family test parser-introspective for argparse-backed families: derive every live help-backed parser with a populated `_SubParsersAction`, assert that population matches `_NESTED_FAMILY`, then prove each `rebar <family> <child> --help` returns child usage. Runtime stays import-isolated while the test detects future membership drift.
- Add a focused `rebar config validate --help` contract proving the handler-dispatched pseudo-subcommand reaches `build_validate` and returns validate child help rather than the committed top-level `config` artifact; this case is explicit because parser introspection cannot discover it.
- Add concise parser `description=` values to the four pure-intercept factories that currently lack them: `reconcile.build`, `enrich.build`, `identity.build`, and `certs.build_trusted_env`. These route-owned descriptions supply overview one-liners without registry prose.
- Move `_unwrap_usage` and `_collapse_metavars` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` into `scripts/gen_cli_help.py`. In `render_route`, apply `_unwrap_usage` only when `route.group == "intercept"` and `parser.usage is None`; apply `_collapse_metavars` to intercept option-invocation lines before existing byte normalization.
- Pin the explicit-usage exception with `trusted-env`: its author-supplied `add` and `revoke` usage forms remain on separate lines. Other pure-intercept artifacts normalize argparse-generated usage across Python versions.
- Generate one committed `help/<route>.txt` artifact for each newly help-backed intercept route. Existing `_help.py` file lookup, `subcommand_help`, and `known_subcommands` serve those files without a second renderer.
- Let `_help_route.pre_scan` serve top-level pure-intercept help through the widened predicate. The expanded nested-family set preserves child-help ownership for `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, `workflow`, plus the existing bridge family.
- Delete `_render_intercept` from `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`; make `_syntax_body` require `help_mod.subcommand_help(route.name)` for every documented route.
- Migrate both direct `_render_intercept` consumers in `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py` to the committed `review-plan` body. Confirm zero remaining semantic or string references repository-wide.
- Retain `_OVERVIEW_OMIT` as exactly `bridge-fsck` and `bridge-probe`. Retain the matching test allowlist as exactly `help`, `bridge-fsck`, and `bridge-probe`; no pure-intercept route is exempt.
- Keep `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_parser_formatter_pinned.py` scoped away from pure-intercept parsers and update its rationale: generator normalization permits those parsers to retain stdlib `HelpFormatter`.
- Regenerate package help, overview help, and the CLI reference through the existing generators. The existing `_build-and-test.yml` Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 cells each run the help drift check against the same committed bytes.
- Add registry-driven coverage for all pure-intercept routes, both top-level help surfaces, factory-summary completeness, reference consumption, explicit multiline usage, every derived argparse nested-family fallthrough case, and the explicit handler-dispatched `config validate --help` case.
- Do not add another router, parser, help source, mechanical writing-policy gate, or change to the Markdown-only reduced test policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every live visible route outside the exact documented overview omit set appears exactly once in overview help.
- [ ] `rebar help <command>` succeeds for every canonical pure-intercept route returned by the registry.
- [ ] The registry-driven pure-intercept help test proves no command handler executes.
- [ ] The registry-driven pure-intercept help test proves no ticket store is mounted or created.
- [ ] `rebar help <command>` returns the exact matching committed artifact bytes.
- [ ] Top-level `rebar <command> --help` returns the exact matching committed artifact bytes.
- [ ] Every pure-intercept parser factory supplies a non-blank overview description.
- [ ] The committed `trusted-env` usage banner preserves separate `add` and `revoke` lines.
- [ ] Existing Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 matrix cells each pass `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check`.
- [ ] Each CLI-reference pure-intercept syntax block equals the matching committed artifact.
- [ ] A repository-wide semantic-plus-string search reports zero `_render_intercept` references.
- [ ] All four help-backed census sites use the live-visible predicate.
- [ ] The exact overview exemptions remain `help`, `bridge-fsck`, `bridge-probe`.
- [ ] Hidden aliases remain absent from overview discovery.
- [ ] Retired spellings remain absent from overview discovery.
- [ ] `_NESTED_INTERCEPTS` equals `audit`, `config`, `identity`, `llm`, `prompt`, `criteria`, `workflow`.
- [ ] The parameterized nested-family test returns child-parser usage for every parser-introspectable derived member.
- [ ] `rebar config validate --help` reaches `build_validate` and returns validate child help rather than top-level config help.
- [ ] The help drift check passes.
- [ ] The CLI-reference drift check passes.
- [ ] No competing routing, parser, or help mechanism is introduced.
- [ ] No mechanical writing enforcement is introduced.
- [ ] The Markdown-only reduced test policy remains unchanged.
